correctness.rationale: The exact weighted Fourier-energy identity follows by the planar zonotope determinant formula and the uniformly convergent Fourier series of absolute sine; its diagonal cancellations and all factors were checked directly. The triangular-array Lindeberg theorem yields independent circular Gaussian spectral modes under explicit diffuseness, and an exact expected Fourier tail rho_n/[pi(2M+1)] proves passage to the full series. The iid finite-second-moment special case follows from laws of large numbers and a maximal-weight estimate; the spike example follows from a noncentral Gaussian mode with a rotationally invariant shared phase. Finite-n mean/variance follow from complete orthogonality of centered pair kernels. The standalone code, replayed from the current package path, checks hull area, perimeter, Fourier normalization, and sample Laplace transforms but does not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The new contribution is the exact perimeter-normalized stochastic area-deficit law for every diffuse deterministic length array, its arbitrary positive iid-length universality with one moment-ratio parameter, and the explicit noncentral spectral obstruction from one central-limit-scale segment. Schneider (arXiv:2202.06774, sections 3–4) gives general valuation expectations and a nondegenerate first-order CLT, not these second-order shape limits. Joós–Lángi (arXiv:2206.03204, section 4) give deterministic isoperimetric bounds and expected areas, not a limiting probability law. Buffière–Marchal use a lattice sampling model. An existing fixed-body equal-weight random-rotation law covers related spectral fluctuations, but does not include independent random lengths or the one-spike boundary. Classical circular Sobolev statistics encompass related unweighted spectral methods and are acknowledged; their methods are not claimed new. The indexed literature and directly compared closest published records do not state or imply the deterministic diffuse universality plus explicit one-spike separation. Priority is provisional because the complete 1975 source is inaccessible.

value.rationale: This is a structural geometric-probability law for the shape rather than overall size of random zonotopes: rescaling to a common perimeter reveals non-Gaussian area fluctuations whose entire limiting law depends on arbitrary independent segment lengths through only a single natural moment ratio. The sharp single-spike counterexample shows precisely why diffuseness cannot be omitted and yields a different noncentral spectral law even at the same quadratic weight statistic. The theorem therefore links stochastic convex geometry, angular Fourier energies, and a meaningful universality boundary, not a routine finite numerical exercise.
